fact_reviews.subject: main/melee/lb/lbfile:discIsDone
fact_reviews.old_value: Takes no explicit input. Each invocation first calls `lb_800195D0`, then reloads and returns the shared `cancel` flag; that flag is cleared before the asynchronous DevCom request and set to true by its completion callback, so the returned value carries interrupt-updated request state into the caller's polling condition.
fact_reviews.reason: State only the independently read callback-to-poll data flow.

fact_reviews.subject: main/melee/lb/lbfile:discIsDone

fact_reviews.subject: main/melee/lb/lbfile:discIsDone
fact_reviews.old_value: Services runtime disc and card work during synchronous file polling, then reports whether the asynchronous DVD request completion callback has set the shared completion flag. Its non-inlined call boundary also keeps the polling loop interrupt-observable under MWCC.
fact_reviews.reason: The source includes an MWCC non-inline pragma and an explanatory TODO; that does not independently prove the hardware interrupt mechanism claimed by the old fact.

fact_reviews.subject: main/melee/lb/lbfile:discIsDone
fact_reviews.old_value: The helper has no local branches or state transitions: on every polling iteration it performs one delegated runtime-service step and then samples the shared completion state. Until the asynchronous callback changes `cancel` from false to true, `waitForDisc` repeats; the non-inlined helper boundary permits interrupt execution and prevents MWCC's polling loop from treating the flag as invariant.
fact_reviews.reason: Preserve observed ordering and compilation directive while removing an unverified interrupt-execution guarantee.

fact_reviews.subject: main/melee/lb/lbfile:lbFile_8001615C
fact_reviews.old_value: Receives completion arguments from HSD DevCom, ignores the first three, asserts that the Boolean cancellation argument is false, and asynchronously writes true to lbfile's shared `cancel` completion latch. The foreground wait loop repeatedly calls `discIsDone`, whose non-inlined boundary allows interrupts to run before it returns the latch.
fact_reviews.reason: Remove unsupported claims that the function-call boundary itself permits interrupt execution.

fact_reviews.subject: main/melee/lb/lbfile:lbFile_8001615C

fact_reviews.subject: main/melee/lb/lbfile:lbFile_8001615C

The foreground loop yields to interrupts and polls until it observes that transition. A callback invocation marked as cancelled violates the path's invariant and asserts instead of being accepted as normal completion.
fact_reviews.reason: Describe exact local transitions without asserting a scheduling mechanism.

fact_reviews.subject: main/melee/lb/lbfile:lbFile_800168A0
fact_reviews.old_value: A preload-cache hit returns immediately with `true` and does not alter the unit's completion latch. A miss clears the shared `cancel` latch, submits one DevCom request with `lbFile_8001615C` as its completion callback, and waits without a timeout through `waitForDisc`, whose `discIsDone` poll services the lower-level disc subsystem until the callback asserts that the request was not cancelled and changes the latch to true; only then does the function return `false`. Thus both normal return paths provide usable data, and the Boolean distinguishes cached reuse from fallback loading rather than success from failure.
fact_reviews.reason: Remove guarantees that every miss transparently falls back and every normal path independently validates a usable pointer.
